title: No Self and Nirvana
objective: After this level you can explain why Buddhists teach that nothing is permanent and there is no fixed self, and what nirvana means.
summary: Buddhists teach impermanence, suffering and no-self: a person is five changing factors. Nirvana, the "blowing out" of desire, hatred and ignorance, ends suffering and rebirth.

cards.headline: Are you the same person you were at five?
cards.body: Your body, your moods and your opinions have all changed since then. Buddhist teaching takes that question seriously, and it leads somewhere surprising: to no fixed self at all, and to nirvana.

cards.headline: Three marks of everything
cards.body: Buddhist teaching names three characteristics of all existence. Anicca: impermanence. Dukkha: suffering, Level 52's first truth. And anatta: no-self. Buddhists teach that there is in humans no permanent, underlying substance that can be called a soul. A person is five factors, the skandhas, all constantly changing. Less a stone, more a river.

cards.headline: Blowing out the flame
cards.body: Nirvana literally means "blowing out", the way a flame is blown out. What goes out is desire, hatred and ignorance, and in the end suffering and rebirth themselves. So nirvana is not a place. It is an absence, above all the absence of suffering.

mascot.line: Common mix-up: nirvana isn't a heaven you travel to. Picture a flame going out, not a door opening.

cards.headline: Nirvana in life, and at death
cards.body: Buddhists distinguish two kinds. Nirvana can be reached in this life, while the body carries on. Final nirvana comes at death, when the causes of any future existence have been extinguished. Buddhists hold that the Buddha entered it when he died at Kushinagar, never to be born again.

cards.headline: No Self and Nirvana: the takeaways
learned: Everything is impermanent, unsatisfying and without a fixed self
A person is five changing factors
Nirvana means "blowing out": the end of suffering and rebirth

questions.explanation: Nirvana means "blowing out", as a flame is blown out.

questions.prompt: Match each Buddhist term with its meaning.
questions.explanation: Anicca is impermanence, dukkha is suffering, anatta is no-self, and nirvana literally means "blowing out".

questions.prompt: Level 8 said much of the Indian family shares karma, rebirth and the hope of release. Where does nirvana fit?

options.label: It is the best realm to be reborn into
options.rationale: It isn't a place, and it ends rebirth.

options.label: It is the Buddhist release from suffering and rebirth
It is another word for karma
options.rationale: Karma shapes future lives; nirvana ends rebirth.

options.label: It is a festival held each spring
options.rationale: That would be a holiday, not release.

questions.explanation: Nirvana is the extinction of desire, hatred and ignorance, and ultimately of suffering and rebirth: Buddhism's form of release.
